metaTitle: Light Fixture Installation in Los Angeles | $135–$235
metaDescription: Swapping or adding a light fixture in an LA home? See what drives the $135–$235 cost, what a licensed electrician does, and when to call one.
intro: That new pendant or ceiling fixture sitting in its box isn't going to hang itself, and in Los Angeles homes the wiring behind the wall can be anywhere from decades-old cloth-wrapped wire in a pre-war bungalow to fresh Romex in a new-build apartment. Getting the fixture mounted safely and wired correctly matters more than it looks, since a loose connection or mismatched wire can cause flickering, buzzing, or a fire hazard down the line.
causes: An old fixture has failed or gone out of style and needs to be swapped for a new one.
A room like a nursery, dining area, or home office never had overhead lighting installed.
A mid-century home has outdated wiring or a junction box that isn't rated for the new fixture's weight.
A pre-war bungalow has old cloth wiring or no ground wire, which complicates a straightforward swap.
A new-build apartment has a fixture pre-wired but the buyer wants a different style installed.
whatProDoes: Shuts off power to the circuit at the breaker and confirms it's dead with a voltage tester before touching any wires.
Removes the old fixture (if present) and inspects the junction box for damage, proper grounding, and weight rating.
Connects the new fixture's wires to the household wiring using wire nuts, matching hot, neutral, and ground correctly.
Secures the fixture to the junction box or ceiling brace, making sure it can support the fixture's weight long-term.
Restores power and tests the fixture, checking for flickering, buzzing, or loose connections before wrapping up.
diyOrPro: If you're replacing a fixture with an identical mounting style and the power is confirmed off, some homeowners handle simple swaps themselves. But if your home has older wiring, no ground wire, a fixture heavier than a standard light, or you're adding a new circuit where none existed, call a licensed electrician — miswired connections or an unsupported junction box can lead to shock, fire, or a fixture falling.
priceNote: This job runs $135 to $235 in Los Angeles, based on a $100/hour rate for a typical 1-2 hour job. Older homes with outdated wiring, hard-to-reach ceilings, or fixtures requiring a new junction box tend to land toward the higher end of that range.

faqs.q: Do I need an electrician for a simple fixture swap, or can I do it myself?
faqs.a: A straightforward one-for-one swap with the power off is manageable for some homeowners, but if you're unsure about the wiring, grounding, or box rating, it's safer to have a licensed electrician handle it.

faqs.q: Will the price change if there's no existing wiring for the fixture?
faqs.a: The $135 to $235 range covers standard installation where wiring already exists; running new wiring or adding a switch is a separate job and would be quoted differently.

faqs.q: My house is from the 1930s — is that a problem for a new fixture?
faqs.a: Older homes sometimes have cloth wiring or ungrounded junction boxes, which an electrician needs to check before installing anything; this is common in LA's pre-war bungalows and doesn't necessarily change the price, but it does need to be inspected first.
